note: Re-judged 2026-10-24 (independent auditor, authored none of the change). RFC 9136 Section 3.1: "* The Ethernet Segment Identifier MUST be a non-zero 10-octet identifier if the ESI is used as an Overlay Index (see the definition of "Overlay Index" in Section 3.2). It MUST be all bytes zero otherwise." 238bdb62e9 only renamed ParseESIString to parseESIString in the cited encode.go::l2vpnRouteToEVPNParams; the overlay-index guard and the ESI handling the verdict rests on are unchanged, and the tagged carriers are byte-identical. Verdict unchanged: enforced. Earlier judgement follows. Re-judged 2026-10-19 (independent auditor, after 4283f8d2e3). Verdict stands: enforced. RFC 9136 Section 3.1: "The Ethernet Segment Identifier MUST be a non-zero 10-octet identifier if the ESI is used as an Overlay Index (see the definition of "Overlay Index" in Section 3.2).  It MUST be all bytes zero otherwise." No producer change since 0411b53e91 (git log over internal/component/bgp/plugins/nlri/evpn and update_text_evpn.go shows only 4283f8d2e3, which touches internal/le/interoplab/bgp/check_extras.go alone). checkOverlayIndex is unchanged and still the only gate before newEVPNType5, whose two non-test callers (plugin.go buildEVPNFromParams, encode.go l2vpnRouteToEVPNParams) both call it first. Tagged units pass at HEAD (go test -run 'TestRFC9136Overlay|EVPNType5ESIGateway' over nlri/evpn and cmd/update, ok). Interop, closing the prior note's owed item: 4283f8d2e3 makes bgp-evpn-gobgp originate through update text ('... ip-prefix rd 1:1 esi 00:01:02:03:04:05:06:07:08:09 etag 0 prefix 10.77.0.0/24 overlay-index esi label 0', internal/le/interoplab/bgp/helper.go:202, path parseEVPNSection -> buildEVPNFromParams -> checkOverlayIndex) and wait for GoBGP's JSON NLRI to read "esi":"ESI_ARBITRARY | 01:02:03:04:05:06:07:08:09","etag":0,"prefix":"10.77.0.0/24","gateway":"0.0.0.0". bgp-evpn-frr now only asserts FRR keyed the route [5]:[0]:[24]:[10.77.0.0] (FRR 10.3.1 prints no type-5 ESI), so FRR proves acceptance, not the octets. Both scenarios reported 1 passed in the commit body; not re-run by this judge. Red recorded in the commit body: a GOFLAGS overlay passing ESI{} to newEVPNType5 in buildEVPNFromParams made bgp-evpn-gobgp fail its assertion 3 (GoBGP read esi single-homed), so the interop discriminates the non-zero-when-index clause at a second implementation. The zero-otherwise clause and every refusal remain unit-proven only (TestRFC9136OverlayIndexESIRefusedOtherwise, four mutants each red on its own subtest per the 2026-10-18 note); an interop peer cannot observe a route Ze refuses to send, so no interop negative is owed. The interop check is untagged reach/goal evidence and adds no tag; it carries no discrimination record of its own under ./le rfc discriminate-record, only the commit-body red.
